```{r}

 
## -------------------------------------------------
## 0) Setup
## -------------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)


knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

packages <- c(
  "readxl", "dplyr", "readr", "lavaan", "semTools", "lubridate",
  "stringr", "tidyr", "Hmisc", "ggplot2", "moments", "patchwork",
  "mice", "lmtest", "car", "tools", "lme4", "miceadds", "DescTools",
  "psych", "performance"
)

installed <- packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())
if (any(!installed)) install.packages(packages[!installed])
suppressPackageStartupMessages(
  invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE))
)

## -------------------------------------------------
## Output layout
## -------------------------------------------------
## run_analysis.sh writes everything this document prints to
## results/analysis.log. section() opens each part of that log with a numbered
## banner naming the part of the paper it supports; claim() marks the line(s) a
## reported value is read from. Both only print; neither touches the analysis.
section <- local({
  n <- 0
  function(title, paper, note = NULL) {
    n <<- n + 1
    rule <- strrep("#", 80)
    cat("\n\n", rule, "\n", sprintf("### %d. %s\n", n, title),
        sprintf("###    Paper: %s\n", paper), sep = "")
    if (!is.null(note)) cat(paste0("###    ", strwrap(note, 72), "\n"), sep = "")
    cat(rule, "\n\n", sep = "")
  }
})
## A claim longer than about 100 characters continues on indented lines, so
## '>>> ' still marks where each one starts.
claim <- function(...) {
  lines <- strwrap(paste0(...), width = 100, prefix = "    ", initial = ">>> ")
  lines <- gsub("([.?!])  ", "\\1 ", lines)  # strwrap doubles the space after a full stop
  cat("\n", paste0(lines, "\n"), sep = "")
}
## Tables print at their full width rather than wrapping their columns into
## further blocks at R's default 80 characters.
options(width = 10000)


## -------------------------------------------------
## 1) Read raw data
## -------------------------------------------------

df_raw <- read_excel("study_data_merged.xlsx")


num_cols <- c(
  "Optimism_bias_self_1", "Optimism_bias_self_2",
  "Optimism_bias_other_1", "Optimism_bias_other_2",
  paste0("self_efficacy_", 1:4),
  paste0("risk_perception_", 1:6),
  paste0("locus_of_control_", 1:12),
  paste0("Acceptance _", 1:8),
  paste0("negative_emotions_", 1:13),
  paste0("Training intention _", 1:5),
  paste0("Q21_", 1:3),
  paste0("Q22_", 1:2)
)


section("Sample construction",
        "Section 3.2.1 (Sample)",
        note = paste(
          "Naming used throughout the code and this log: sim0, sim0.5, sim1 and",
          "sim2 are the paper's simulations 1, 2, 3 and 4."))

claim("Section 3.2.1: 1625 recorded responses, 138 duplicate exclusions")
cat("Recorded responses:", nrow(df_raw), "\n")
cat("Raw duplicates (by anonymisedEmail): ",
    sum(duplicated(df_raw$anonymisedEmail)), "\n")


## -------------------------------------------------
## 2) Parse numerics + reverse code
## -------------------------------------------------

rev_items <- paste0("locus_of_control_", c(1,2,6,7,8,9,10,11))

df_clean <- df_raw %>%
  mutate(
    across(all_of(num_cols), ~ parse_number(as.character(.))),
    across(all_of(rev_items), ~ 8 - .)
  )


## -------------------------------------------------
## 3) Check: t-Test for duplicated values --> different? 
##    Remove duplicates
##    Rule: take first occurrence per anonymisedEmail
## -------------------------------------------------
dup_emails <- df_clean %>%
  count(anonymisedEmail) %>%
  filter(n > 1) %>%
  pull(anonymisedEmail)

if (length(dup_emails) > 0) {
  
  df_dup <- df_clean %>%
    filter(anonymisedEmail %in% dup_emails) %>%
    mutate(
      optimism_bias =
        rowMeans(across(c(Optimism_bias_other_1, Optimism_bias_other_2)),
                 na.rm = TRUE) -
        rowMeans(across(c(Optimism_bias_self_1,  Optimism_bias_self_2)),
                 na.rm = TRUE),
      self_efficacy      = rowMeans(across(self_efficacy_1:self_efficacy_4), na.rm = TRUE),
      risk_perception    = rowMeans(across(c(risk_perception_1:risk_perception_4,
                                             risk_perception_6)),
                                    na.rm = TRUE),
      locus_of_control   = rowMeans(across(locus_of_control_1:locus_of_control_12),
                                    na.rm = TRUE),
      acceptance         = rowMeans(across(c(`Acceptance _1`:`Acceptance _6`,
                                             `Acceptance _8`)),
                                    na.rm = TRUE),
      negative_emotions  = rowMeans(across(c(negative_emotions_1:negative_emotions_10,
                                             negative_emotions_12:negative_emotions_13)),
                                    na.rm = TRUE),
      training_intention = rowMeans(across(`Training intention _1`:`Training intention _5`),
                                    na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    group_by(anonymisedEmail) %>%
    mutate(entry = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  df_wide <- df_dup %>%
    dplyr::select(anonymisedEmail, entry,
           optimism_bias, self_efficacy, risk_perception,
           locus_of_control, acceptance, negative_emotions,
           training_intention) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from  = entry,
      values_from = c(optimism_bias, self_efficacy, risk_perception,
                      locus_of_control, acceptance, negative_emotions,
                      training_intention),
      names_sep = "_entry"
    )
  
  test_vars <- c("optimism_bias", "self_efficacy", "risk_perception",
                 "locus_of_control", "acceptance", "negative_emotions",
                 "training_intention")
  
  paired_results <- lapply(test_vars, function(var) {
    v1 <- paste0(var, "_entry1")
    v2 <- paste0(var, "_entry2")
    t_res <- t.test(df_wide[[v1]], df_wide[[v2]], paired = TRUE)
    data.frame(
      variable  = var,
      t_stat    = unname(t_res$statistic),
      df        = unname(t_res$parameter),
      p_value   = unname(t_res$p.value),
      mean_diff = mean(df_wide[[v1]] - df_wide[[v2]], na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  })
  
  paired_results_df <- bind_rows(paired_results)
  claim("Not reported in the paper: paired t-tests comparing the two entries of each duplicate")
  cat("\nPaired t-tests duplicate entries (pre-dedupe):\n")
  print(paired_results_df)
}


## -------------------------------------------------
## 4) Remove duplicates (exluding the second value)
## -------------------------------------------------
df_dedup <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(anonymisedEmail) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("Unique participants after dedupe: ", nrow(df_dedup), "\n")


## -------------------------------------------------
## 5) Attention checks
##    We'll compute all variants once.
## -------------------------------------------------

# Helper: number of passed checks per row
df_checks <- df_dedup %>%
  mutate(
    pass1 = risk_perception_5    == 1,
    pass2 = `Acceptance _7`      == 3,
    pass3 = negative_emotions_11 == 1,
    n_pass = rowSums(cbind(pass1, pass2, pass3), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

n_total <- nrow(df_checks)

### 4a) strict = all 3 correct
df_strict <- df_checks %>%
  filter(
    risk_perception_5    == 1,
    `Acceptance _7`      == 3,
    negative_emotions_11 == 1
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-pass1, -pass2, -pass3, -n_pass)

claim("Section 3.2.1: 419 attention-check exclusions: 'Excluded' under [Strict check]. ",
      "The two looser rules after it are shown for comparison and were not used")
cat("\n[Strict check]\n")
cat(" Kept:        ", nrow(df_strict), "\n")
cat(" Excluded:    ", n_total - nrow(df_strict), "\n")
cat(" Excluded %:  ",
    round(100 * (n_total - nrow(df_strict)) / n_total, 1), "%\n", sep="")

### 4b) max 2 fails = at least 1 correct  (n_pass >= 1)
df_max2fail <- df_checks %>%
  filter(n_pass >= 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(-pass1, -pass2, -pass3, -n_pass)

cat("\n[Max 2 fails]\n")
cat(" Kept (>=1 ok): ", nrow(df_max2fail), "\n")
cat(" Excluded:      ", n_total - nrow(df_max2fail), "\n")

### 4c) min 2 correct = n_pass >= 2
df_min2pass <- df_checks %>%
  filter(n_pass >= 2) %>%
  dplyr::select(-pass1, -pass2, -pass3, -n_pass)

cat("\n[Min 2 correct]\n")
cat(" Kept (>=2 ok): ", nrow(df_min2pass), "\n")
cat(" Excluded:      ", n_total - nrow(df_min2pass), "\n\n")


## -------------------------------------------------
## Decision for dataset to continue with:
## -------------------------------------------------

df_analysis <- df_strict


##-------------------------------------------------
##Exclusion of those participants who a. did not read or deleted the email
##-------------------------------------------------



to_valid <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  ifelse(is.na(x) | x == "" | x == "--", 0L, 1L)
}

df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis %>%
  mutate(
    read_sim1    = to_valid(sim1_MessageRead_TimeStamp),
    read_sim2    = to_valid(sim2_MessageRead_TimeStamp),
    del_sim1     = to_valid(sim1_MessageDeleted_TimeStamp),
    del_sim2     = to_valid(sim2_MessageDeleted_TimeStamp),
    processed_sim1 = ifelse(read_sim1 == 1L | del_sim1 == 1L, 1L, 0L),
    processed_sim2 = ifelse(read_sim2 == 1L | del_sim2 == 1L, 1L, 0L)
  ) %>%
  filter(processed_sim1 == 1L, processed_sim2 == 1L)



claim("Section 3.2.1: final N = 986. The paper gives 86 exclusions for opening or deleting neither simulation 3 nor 4; ",
      "the data give 82 (see PROVENANCE.md)")
cat("N before exposure filter:", nrow(df_analysis), "\n")
cat("N after exposure filter: ", nrow(df_analysis_filt), "\n")
cat("Excluded:                ", nrow(df_analysis) - nrow(df_analysis_filt), "\n")





##-------------------------------------------------
## 6) Straightlining
##-------------------------------------------------

section("Straightlining check",
        "not reported",
        note = "A data-quality check. Nobody is excluded on it: every later analysis uses the full N = 986.")

 
items_all <- c(
  "Optimism_bias_self_1","Optimism_bias_self_2",
  "Optimism_bias_other_1","Optimism_bias_other_2",
  paste0("self_efficacy_", 1:4),
  paste0("risk_perception_", 1:6),
  paste0("locus_of_control_", 1:12),          
  paste0("Acceptance _", 1:8),
  paste0("negative_emotions_", 1:13),
  paste0("Training intention _", 1:5),
  paste0("Q21_", 1:3), paste0("Q22_", 1:2)
)

 
.longstring_vec <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA_integer_)
  s <- split(x, cumsum(is.na(x)))                      
  runs <- unlist(lapply(s, function(v) if (length(v)) rle(v)$lengths else integer()))
  if (length(runs)) max(runs) else 0L
}
.n_runs_ge_x <- function(x, X = 12) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA_integer_)
  s <- split(x, cumsum(is.na(x)))
  runs <- unlist(lapply(s, function(v) if (length(v)) rle(v)$lengths else integer()))
  sum(runs >= X)
}
.prop_same_adj <- function(x) {
  v <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(v) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  mean(v[-1] == v[-length(v)])
}
.irv <- function(x) {
  v <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(v) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  stats::sd(v)
}

 
 
scale01 <- function(v) {
  if (all(is.na(v))) return(v)
  vnum <- as.numeric(v)
  vmin <- 1
  vmax <- max(vnum, na.rm = TRUE)
  out <- (vnum - vmin) / (vmax - vmin)
  round(out, 2)                                     
}

df_seq <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  dplyr::select(anonymisedEmail, all_of(items_all)) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(items_all), scale01))


 
threshold_X <- 12

straight_all <- df_seq |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    longstring_all    = .longstring_vec(dplyr::c_across(dplyr::all_of(items_all))),
    n_runs_ge_12_all  = .n_runs_ge_x(dplyr::c_across(dplyr::all_of(items_all)), X = threshold_X),
    prop_same_adj_all = .prop_same_adj(dplyr::c_across(dplyr::all_of(items_all))),
    irv_all           = .irv(dplyr::c_across(dplyr::all_of(items_all))),
    flag_ge_12_all    = longstring_all >= threshold_X
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(anonymisedEmail, longstring_all, n_runs_ge_12_all,
                prop_same_adj_all, irv_all, flag_ge_12_all)

 
straight_all |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(longstring_all)) |>
  print(n = 20)

 
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggplot2")


 
ggplot(straight_all, aes(x = longstring_all)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, color = "black", fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    stat = "count",
    aes(label = ..count..),
    vjust = -0.3,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of LongString values across all items",
    x = "Longest series with same answer",
    y = "Frequency (number of persons)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

 
straight_all %>%
  filter(longstring_all >= 12) %>%
  dplyr::select(anonymisedEmail, longstring_all, irv_all) %>%
  arrange(desc(longstring_all))

## -------------------------------------------------
## Alternative dataset without extreme straightliners (cutoff ≥ 18)
## -------------------------------------------------


straightliner_ids <- straight_all %>%
  filter(longstring_all >= 18) %>%
  pull(anonymisedEmail)

cat("\nStraightliners (>= 18 identical answers in a row): ",
    length(straightliner_ids), "\n")


df_analysis_filt_noSL <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  filter(!anonymisedEmail %in% straightliner_ids)

cat("N Original (df_analysis_filt): ", nrow(df_analysis_filt), "\n")
cat("N without straightliners    : ", nrow(df_analysis_filt_noSL), "\n")




## -------------------------------------------------
## 7) Create composite scores on analysis sample
## -------------------------------------------------

section("Scale scores, simulation outcomes and missing data",
        "not reported directly (supporting output)",
        note = paste(
          "Job-role labels, per-simulation click (clicked_*), credential",
          "(compromised_*) and reporting (reported_*) indicators, and the",
          "number of missing values per psychological scale."))

df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
    optimism_bias =
      rowMeans(across(c(Optimism_bias_other_1, Optimism_bias_other_2)),
               na.rm = TRUE) -
      rowMeans(across(c(Optimism_bias_self_1,  Optimism_bias_self_2)),
               na.rm = TRUE),

    self_efficacy      = rowMeans(across(self_efficacy_1:self_efficacy_4), na.rm = TRUE),
    risk_perception    = rowMeans(across(c(risk_perception_1:risk_perception_4,
                                           risk_perception_6)),
                                  na.rm = TRUE),
    locus_of_control   = rowMeans(across(locus_of_control_1:locus_of_control_12),
                                  na.rm = TRUE),
    acceptance         = rowMeans(across(c(`Acceptance _1`:`Acceptance _6`,
                                           `Acceptance _8`)),
                                  na.rm = TRUE),
    negative_emotions  = rowMeans(across(c(negative_emotions_1:negative_emotions_10,
                                           negative_emotions_12:negative_emotions_13)),
                                  na.rm = TRUE),
    training_intention = rowMeans(across(`Training intention _1`:`Training intention _5`),
                                  na.rm = TRUE),
    per_orga_security  = rowMeans(across(Q21_1:Q21_3), na.rm = TRUE),
    feeling_attacked   = rowMeans(across(Q22_1:Q22_2), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

unique(df_analysis_filt$JobRole_std)


## -------------------------------------------------
## 8) Simulation behaviour indicators
##    clicked / compromised / reported across all sims
## -------------------------------------------------

to_indicator <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x) | x == "" ~ NA_integer_,
    x == "--"          ~ 0L,
    TRUE               ~ 1L
  )
}

df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
    # clicked
    clicked_sim0  = to_indicator(`sim0_Viewed Landing Page_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
    clicked_sim05 = to_indicator(`sim0.5_Viewed Landing Page_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),
    clicked_sim1  = to_indicator(sim1_EmailLinkClicked_TimeStamp),
    clicked_sim2  = to_indicator(sim2_EmailLinkClicked_TimeStamp),
    clicked       = clicked_sim0 + clicked_sim05 + clicked_sim1 + clicked_sim2,

    # compromised
    compromised_sim0  = to_indicator(`sim0_Data Entered_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
    compromised_sim05 = to_indicator(`sim0.5_Data Entered_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),
    compromised_sim1  = to_indicator(sim1_CredSupplied_TimeStamp_Compromised),
    compromised_sim2  = to_indicator(sim2_CredSupplied_TimeStamp_Compromised),
    compromised       = compromised_sim0 + compromised_sim05 +
                        compromised_sim1 + compromised_sim2,

    # reported
    reported_sim1 = to_indicator(sim1_Phishing_Reported_On),
    reported_sim2 = to_indicator(sim2_Phishing_Reported_On),
    reported      = reported_sim1 + reported_sim2
  )


invisible(lapply(
  c("clicked_sim0","clicked_sim05","clicked_sim1","clicked_sim2",
    "compromised_sim0","compromised_sim05","compromised_sim1","compromised_sim2",
    "reported_sim1","reported_sim2"),
  \(v) { cat("\n", v, "\n"); print(table(df_analysis_filt[[v]], useNA="ifany")) }
))





## -------------------------------------------------
## 9) Missingness check for key predictors
## -------------------------------------------------

key_preds <- c("optimism_bias", "risk_perception", "negative_emotions",
               "acceptance", "self_efficacy", "locus_of_control")

n_complete <- sum( complete.cases(df_analysis_filt[ key_preds ]) )
cat("\nComplete cases for predictors: ", n_complete, "\n")

df_analysis_filt %>% summarise(n_missing_locus = sum(is.na(locus_of_control))) %>% print()
df_analysis_filt %>% summarise(n_missing_opt   = sum(is.na(optimism_bias)))  %>% print()
df_analysis_filt %>% summarise(n_missing_rp1   = sum(is.na(risk_perception_1))) %>% print()
df_analysis_filt %>% summarise(n_missing_se    = sum(is.na(self_efficacy)))  %>% print()
df_analysis_filt %>% summarise(n_missing_ne    = sum(is.na(negative_emotions))) %>% print()
df_analysis_filt %>% summarise(n_missing_acc   = sum(is.na(acceptance))) %>% print()


## -------------------------------------------------
## 10) Correlations between composites + behaviour
## -------------------------------------------------

section("Correlations between the scales",
        "Appendix D, Table 3")

corr_vars <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  dplyr::select(
    optimism_bias, self_efficacy, risk_perception, locus_of_control,
    acceptance, negative_emotions, training_intention,
    per_orga_security, feeling_attacked
  )

corr_matrix <- cor(corr_vars, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")


res <- rcorr(as.matrix(corr_vars), type = "pearson")
Rmat <- res$r
Pmat <- res$P

stars <- symnum(
  Pmat, corr = FALSE, na = FALSE,
  cutpoints = c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
  symbols   = c("***", "**", "*", " ")
)

Rstars <- matrix(
  paste0(formatC(Rmat, format = "f", digits = 2), stars),
  ncol = ncol(Rmat),
  dimnames = dimnames(Rmat)
)

claim("Table 3: the first seven rows and columns of the matrix below")
cat("\nCorrelation matrix with sig stars:\n")
print(Rstars)

df_analysis_filt %>%

##--------------------------------------------------

##--------------------------------------------------

sim_summary <- tibble(
  sim = c("sim0", "sim0.5", "sim1", "sim2"),
  clicked_rate = c(
    mean(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim0,  na.rm = TRUE),

  compromised_rate = c(

##----------------------------------
## 13) Age and Job role stats
##----------------------------------

section("Age and job role",
        "Section 3.2.1 (Sample)")

## The top band in the datais labelled "65+", not "65-74". Recoding "65-74"
## matched nothing, so dplyr::recode returned NA for those participants and
## mean(..., na.rm = TRUE) silently dropped them from the age statistics.
## Chunk options set warning = FALSE, so nothing was printed either.
df_analysis_filt$age_mean <- dplyr::recode(df_analysis_filt$Age,
  "18-24" = 21,
  "25-34" = 29.5,
  "35-44" = 39.5,
  "45-54" = 49.5,
  "55-64" = 59.5,
  "65+"   = 69.5   # open-ended band; 69.5 assumes an effective 65-74 span
)

## Guard: an unmatched level must never again pass silently.
stopifnot(!any(is.na(df_analysis_filt$age_mean) & !is.na(df_analysis_filt$Age)))


claim("Section 3.2.1 gives mean age 39.3 (SD 10.4), from a recode that dropped the oldest age band. ",
      "Corrected, the data give the two numbers below, 39.8 (SD 11.0); see README.md, Known limitations")
mean(df_analysis_filt$age_mean, na.rm = TRUE)

sd(df_analysis_filt$age_mean, na.rm = TRUE)

df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
    JobRole_bin = factor(
      ifelse(JobRole_std == "academic",
             "academic",
             "non-academic"),
      levels = c("academic", "non-academic")
    )
  )




claim("Section 3.2.1: 455 academic, 531 non-academic")
table(df_analysis_filt$JobRole_bin)

levels(df_analysis_filt$JobRole_bin)


prop.table(table(df_analysis_filt$JobRole_std))


##-----------------------------------
## 14) Reporting
##-----------------------------------

section("Reporting of simulations 3 and 4",
        "not reported",
        note = "Percentages, then counts and rates, of participants who reported the simulated email.")
df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
    reporting_sim1  = to_indicator(sim1_Phishing_Reported_On),
    reporting_sim2  = to_indicator(sim2_Phishing_Reported_On),
```

#Hypothesis 1: Level of compromise
```{r}


## -------------------------------------------------
## Mediation: level_compromised_sim1 → mediators → level_compromised_sim2
## -------------------------------------------------

section("H1: parallel mediation, compromise level in simulation 3 -> simulation 4",
        "Section 4.2 (RQ1, 'Preregistered analysis H1'); Table 4 (tab:H1_indirect)",
        note = paste(
          "level_compromised_sim1 and _sim2 are the compromise levels (0 no click,",
          "1 clicked, 2 entered credentials) in simulations 3 and 4."))

df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
   
    Gender= factor(Gender),
    age = factor(
      Age,
      levels = c("18-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65+"),
      ordered = TRUE
    ),
    age_num = as.numeric(age),

    gender_bin = case_when(
      tolower(as.character(Gender)) %in% c("female", "f", "weiblich") ~ 1,
      tolower(as.character(Gender)) %in% c("male", "m", "männlich")   ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

  
    jobrole_bin01 = ifelse(JobRole_bin == "non-academic", 1, 0),

    clicked_sim1     = as.numeric(clicked_sim1),
    clicked_sim2     = as.numeric(clicked_sim2),
    compromised_sim1 = as.numeric(compromised_sim1),
    compromised_sim2 = as.numeric(compromised_sim2),

    level_compromised_sim1 = case_when(
      compromised_sim1 == 1 ~ 2L,
      clicked_sim1     == 1 ~ 1L,
      TRUE                  ~ 0L
    ),
    level_compromised_sim2 = case_when(
      compromised_sim2 == 1 ~ 2L,
      clicked_sim2     == 1 ~ 1L,
      TRUE                  ~ 0L
    )
  )

table(
  JobRole = ifelse(df_analysis$jobrole_bin01 == 1,
                   "Non-academic",
                   "Academic")
)





## -------------------------------------------------
## Mediation: level_compromised_sim1 → mediators → level_compromised_sim2
## -------------------------------------------------
df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
    Gender = factor(Gender),

    age = factor(
      Age,
      levels = c("18-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65+"),
      ordered = TRUE
    ),
    age_num = as.numeric(age),

    gender_bin = case_when(
      tolower(as.character(Gender)) %in% c("female", "f", "weiblich") ~ 1,
      tolower(as.character(Gender)) %in% c("male", "m", "männlich")   ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    jobrole_bin01 = ifelse(JobRole_bin == "non-academic", 1, 0),

    clicked_sim1     = as.numeric(clicked_sim1),
    clicked_sim2     = as.numeric(clicked_sim2),
    compromised_sim1 = as.numeric(compromised_sim1),
    compromised_sim2 = as.numeric(compromised_sim2),

    level_compromised_sim1 = case_when(
      compromised_sim1 == 1 ~ 2L,
      clicked_sim1     == 1 ~ 1L,
      TRUE                  ~ 0L
    ),
    level_compromised_sim2 = case_when(
      compromised_sim2 == 1 ~ 2L,
      clicked_sim2     == 1 ~ 1L,
      TRUE                  ~ 0L
    )
  )


## -------------------------------------------------
## SEM-Model
## -------------------------------------------------

med_model21_job <- '
  # predictor (sim1) to mediator
  optimism_bias     ~ a1*level_compromised_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  risk_perception   ~ a2*level_compromised_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  negative_emotions ~ a3*level_compromised_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  acceptance        ~ a4*level_compromised_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  self_efficacy     ~ a5*level_compromised_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  locus_of_control  ~ a6*level_compromised_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01

  # outcome (sim2)
  level_compromised_sim2 ~ c3*level_compromised_sim1 +
                           b1*optimism_bias + b2*risk_perception +
                           b3*negative_emotions + b4*acceptance +
                           b5*self_efficacy + b6*locus_of_control +
                           age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01

  # indirect effects
  ind1 := a1*b1
  ind2 := a2*b2
  ind3 := a3*b3
  ind4 := a4*b4
  ind5 := a5*b5
  ind6 := a6*b6
  ind_total := ind1 + ind2 + ind3 + ind4 + ind5 + ind6

  # total effect
  total := c3 + ind_total
'


## -------------------------------------------------
## Model fit
## -------------------------------------------------

fit_mediation_job <- sem(
  med_model21_job,
  data = df_analysis_filt,
  estimator = "MLR",
  missing = "ML",
  meanstructure = TRUE
)

claim("Section 4.2: chi^2(15) = 186.06: 'Test statistic' and 'Degrees of freedom', Standard column, under 'Model Test User Model'")
claim("Table 4: the 'Defined Parameters' block at the end. ind1 to ind6 are the indirect paths via optimism bias, ",
      "risk perception, negative emotions, acceptance, self-efficacy and locus of control; beta_std = Std.all, SE = Std.Err. ",
      "Section 4.2's total effect (0.09, SE = 0.04, z = 2.08, p = .038) is the 'total' row, Estimate column")
summary(fit_mediation_job, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)



# ----------------------------------------
# Simple direct model (linear, no mediation)
# ----------------------------------------

df_direct <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
    lvl1 = as.numeric(level_compromised_sim1),
    lvl2 = as.numeric(level_compromised_sim2)
  )

claim("Not reported in the paper: the same association as a plain linear model, without mediators ",
      "(a paragraph on it is commented out in the paper source)")
fit_direct_beta <- lm(
  scale(lvl2) ~ scale(lvl1) + scale(age_num) + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01,
  data = df_direct
)

summary(fit_direct_beta)




```

```{r}
## -------------------------------------------------
## 2) Pairwise test across all four simulation cycles (descriptive + Cochran-Armitage test)
##    For testing if there is a significant trend over time
## -------------------------------------------------

section("Click and compromise rates across the four simulations; Figure 2",
        "Section 4.1; Figure 2 (fig:clicktrend), written to results/fig2_clicktrend.pdf")


count_yes  <- function(x) sum(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
count_no   <- function(x) sum(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
denom_N    <- function(x) sum(!is.na(x))


click_counts <- tibble(
  sim    = c("sim0","sim0.5","sim1","sim2"),
  yes    = c(count_yes(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim0),
             count_yes(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim05),
             count_yes(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim1),
             count_yes(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim2)),
  no     = c(count_no(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim0),
             count_no(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim05),
             count_no(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim1),
             count_no(df_analysis_filt$clicked_sim2))
) %>%
  mutate(
    denom = yes + no,
    pct   = round(100 * yes / denom, 1)
  )

comp_counts <- tibble(
  sim    = c("sim0","sim0.5","sim1","sim2"),
  yes    = c(count_yes(df_analysis_filt$compromised_sim0),
             count_yes(df_analysis_filt$compromised_sim05),
             count_yes(df_analysis_filt$compromised_sim1),
             count_yes(df_analysis_filt$compromised_sim2)),
  no     = c(count_no(df_analysis_filt$compromised_sim0),
             count_no(df_analysis_filt$compromised_sim05),
             count_no(df_analysis_filt$compromised_sim1),
             count_no(df_analysis_filt$compromised_sim2))
) %>%
  mutate(
    denom = yes + no,
    pct   = round(100 * yes / denom, 1)
  )

claim("Section 4.1 and Figure 2: the pct column of the two tables below (sim0, sim0.5, sim1, sim2 = simulations 1-4)")
cat("\nClick rates by simulation:\n")
print(click_counts)

cat("\nCompromise rates by simulation:\n")
print(comp_counts)


pairwise_prop_test <- function(df_counts, label){
  sims <- df_counts$sim
  for(i in 1:(nrow(df_counts)-1)){
    s1 <- df_counts[i, ]
    s2 <- df_counts[i+1, ]
    cat("\n", label, ": ", s1$sim, " vs ", s2$sim, "\n", sep = "")
    
    print(
      prop.test(
        x = c(s1$yes, s2$yes),
        n = c(s1$denom, s2$denom),
        alternative = "less"  
      )
    )
  }
}

claim("Not reported in the paper: one-sided tests between consecutive simulations")
cat("\n--- Pairwise tests for CLICK ---\n")
pairwise_prop_test(click_counts, "Click")

cat("\n--- Pairwise tests for COMPROMISE ---\n")
pairwise_prop_test(comp_counts, "Compromise")
```

#Hypothesis 2: Cybersecurity training intention

```{r}



df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
    cybsafeLinkClicked = as.numeric(cybsafeLinkClicked),
    training_intention = as.numeric(training_intention)
  )

## -------------------------------------------------
## H2a: Mediation model with training_intention as outcome
## -------------------------------------------------

section("H2: parallel mediation, compromise level in simulation 3 -> training intention",
        "Section 4.3 (RQ2, 'Preregistered analysis H2'); Table 5 (tab:H2_indirect); Figure 3 (fig:click1_intention)",
        note = paste(
          "The model is called model_H3a / fit_H3a in the code for historical",
          "reasons; it is H2. As submitted, it uses the binary click indicator",
          "clicked_sim1 where the paper describes the compromise level (see",
          "README.md, Known limitations). Figure 3 is drawn by hand from the",
          "'Regressions' block of this output and is not generated by this document."))

model_H3a <- '
  # a-paths: predictor -> mediators
  optimism_bias     ~ a1*clicked_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  risk_perception   ~ a2*clicked_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  negative_emotions ~ a3*clicked_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  acceptance        ~ a4*clicked_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  self_efficacy     ~ a5*clicked_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01
  locus_of_control  ~ a6*clicked_sim1 + age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01

  # b-paths + direct path
  training_intention ~ c3*clicked_sim1 +
                       b1*optimism_bias +
                       b2*risk_perception +
                       b3*negative_emotions +
                       b4*acceptance +
                       b5*self_efficacy +
                       b6*locus_of_control +
                       age_num + gender_bin + jobrole_bin01

  # indirect effects
  ind1 := a1*b1
  ind2 := a2*b2
  ind3 := a3*b3
  ind4 := a4*b4
  ind5 := a5*b5
  ind6 := a6*b6

  ind_total := ind1 + ind2 + ind3 + ind4 + ind5 + ind6
  total_effect := c3 + ind_total
'


fit_H3a <- sem(
  model_H3a,
  data = df_analysis_filt,
  estimator = "MLR",     
  missing   = "ML",       
  meanstructure = TRUE,
  fixed.x = FALSE
)

claim("Section 4.3: chi^2(15) = 183.05: 'Test statistic', Scaled column (Section 4.2 quotes the Standard one for H1), ",
      "under 'Model Test User Model'")
claim("Table 5: the 'Defined Parameters' block at the end, ind1 to ind6 in the same order as Table 4, then ind_total ",

      "column. Figure 3: the a- and b-paths under 'Regressions'")
summary(
  fit_H3a,
  standardized = TRUE,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  rsquare = TRUE
)
```

#H3: Personality Level Repeat Clicker

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(mice)

section("H3: number of simulations clicked",
        "Section 4.4 (RQ3, 'Preregistered analysis H3'); Table 6 (tab:phishing_glm); Figure 5 (fig:forest_plot_h3)",
        note = paste(
          "Participants confirmed to have received all four simulations (N = 115);",
          "binomial GLM of clicks out of 4, psychological predictors imputed",
          "by predictive mean matching (m = 30), pooled by Rubin's rules."))

## ----------------------------
## Helpers
## ----------------------------


to_delivered <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x) | x == "" ~ 0L,
    x == "--"          ~ 0L,
    TRUE               ~ 1L
  )
}


to_clicked <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x) | x == "" ~ 0L,
    x == "--"          ~ 0L,
    TRUE               ~ 1L
  )
}

## ----------------------------
## 1) Build analysis variables
## ----------------------------

df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
   
    Gender = factor(Gender),
    age = factor(
      Age,
      levels = c("18-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65+"),
      ordered = TRUE
    ),
    age_num = as.numeric(age),

    gender_bin = case_when(
      tolower(as.character(Gender)) %in% c("female", "f", "weiblich") ~ 1,
      tolower(as.character(Gender)) %in% c("male", "m", "männlich")   ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    
    JobRole_bin = as.factor(JobRole_bin),

    
    sent_sim0  = to_delivered(`sim0_Opened_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
    sent_sim05 = to_delivered(`sim0.5_Opened_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),

    
    sent_sim1 = to_delivered(sim1_SuccessfullyDeliveredEmail_TimeStamp),
    sent_sim2 = to_delivered(sim2_SuccessfullyDeliveredEmail_TimeStamp),


    # CLICKED
    clicked_sim0  = to_clicked(`sim0_Viewed Landing Page_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
    clicked_sim05 = to_clicked(`sim0.5_Viewed Landing Page_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),
    clicked_sim1  = to_clicked(sim1_EmailLinkClicked_TimeStamp),
    clicked_sim2  = to_clicked(sim2_EmailLinkClicked_TimeStamp)
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(
    clicked_sim0  = clicked_sim0  * sent_sim0,
    clicked_sim05 = clicked_sim05 * sent_sim05,
    clicked_sim1  = clicked_sim1  * sent_sim1,
    clicked_sim2  = clicked_sim2  * sent_sim2
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_sent    = sent_sim0 + sent_sim05 + sent_sim1 + sent_sim2,
    n_clicked = clicked_sim0 + clicked_sim05 + clicked_sim1 + clicked_sim2,
    click_rate = if_else(n_sent > 0, n_clicked / n_sent, NA_real_)
  )


sum(df_analysis_filt$n_clicked > df_analysis_filt$n_sent, na.rm = TRUE)


df_analysis_filt <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  mutate(
    repeat_clicker = case_when(
      n_sent < 3 ~ NA_integer_,
      n_clicked >= 2 ~ 1L,
      TRUE ~ 0L
    )
  )

table(df_analysis_filt$repeat_clicker, useNA = "ifany")

## ----------------------------
## 2) Complete exposure subset (4/4)
## ----------------------------

df_cc4 <- df_analysis_filt %>%
  filter(sent_sim0 == 1, sent_sim05 == 1, sent_sim1 == 1, sent_sim2 == 1) %>%
  mutate(
    n_sent = 4L,
    n_clicked = clicked_sim0 + clicked_sim05 + clicked_sim1 + clicked_sim2
  )

claim("Section 4.4: repeat-clicking subset N = 115")
cat("N with complete exposure (4/4):", nrow(df_cc4), "\n")

## ----------------------------
## 3) Imputation dataset (predictors only)
##    age_num, gender_bin, JobRole_bin are NOT imputed
## ----------------------------

dat_imp <- df_cc4 %>%
  dplyr::select(
    n_clicked,          
    optimism_bias,
    self_efficacy,
    risk_perception,
    locus_of_control,
    acceptance,
    negative_emotions,
    age_num,            
    gender_bin,         
    JobRole_bin
  )

meth <- make.method(dat_imp)


meth["n_clicked"] <- ""


meth[c("age_num", "gender_bin", "JobRole_bin")] <- ""


meth[c(
  "optimism_bias",
  "self_efficacy",
  "risk_perception",
  "locus_of_control",
  "acceptance",
  "negative_emotions"
)] <- "pmm"

pred <- make.predictorMatrix(dat_imp)
pred[,] <- 1
diag(pred) <- 0


pred["n_clicked", ] <- 0


set.seed(123)
imp <- mice(
  dat_imp,
  m = 30,
  method = meth,
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  maxit = 30,
  printFlag = FALSE
)


zvars <- c("optimism_bias","self_efficacy","risk_perception",
           "locus_of_control","acceptance","negative_emotions","age_num")

fit_imp_z <- with(
  imp,
  {
    d <- data.frame(n_clicked, optimism_bias, self_efficacy, risk_perception,
                    locus_of_control, acceptance, negative_emotions,
                    age_num, gender_bin, JobRole_bin)

    for (v in intersect(zvars, names(d))) {
      d[[v]] <- as.numeric(scale(d[[v]]))
    }

    glm(
      cbind(n_clicked, 4 - n_clicked) ~
        optimism_bias + self_efficacy + risk_perception +
        locus_of_control + acceptance + negative_emotions +
        age_num + gender_bin + JobRole_bin,
      family = binomial(),
      data = d
    )
  }
)

res_z <- pool(fit_imp_z)
claim("Section 4.4 and Table 6: the optimism_bias row, estimate 0.42, std.error 0.18, p .029; ",
      "Table 6 gives estimate and std.error for every row")
summary(res_z)


sum_z <- summary(res_z)

sum_z$OR        <- exp(sum_z$estimate)
sum_z$OR_low95  <- exp(sum_z$estimate - 1.96 * sum_z$std.error)
sum_z$OR_high95 <- exp(sum_z$estimate + 1.96 * sum_z$std.error)

sum_z[, c("term","estimate","std.error","p.value","OR","OR_low95","OR_high95")]



## ============================================================
##  forest plot 
## ============================================================

psych_labels <- c(
  optimism_bias     = "Optimism bias",
  self_efficacy     = "Self-efficacy",
  risk_perception   = "Risk perception",

)

df_plot <- sum_z %>%
  filter(as.character(term) %in% names(psych_labels)) %>%

p <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = OR, y = Predictor)) +

##----------------------

section("Figure 4: participants by number of simulations clicked, and compromise probability per click",
        "Section 4.4; Figure 4 (fig:click_histogram), written to results/fig4_click_histogram.pdf")

local({

  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)

  to_binary_present <- function(x) {
    x <- trimws(as.character(x))
    dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(x) | x == "" ~ 0L,
      x == "--"          ~ 0L,
      TRUE               ~ 1L
    )
  }

  to_clicked <- function(x) {
    x <- trimws(as.character(x))
    dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(x) | x == "" ~ 0L,
      x == "--"          ~ 0L,
      TRUE               ~ 1L
    )
  }

  wilson_ci <- function(x, n, z = 1.96) {
    if (is.na(n) || n == 0) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
    p <- x / n
    denom <- 1 + z^2 / n
    center <- (p + z^2/(2*n)) / denom
    half <- (z * sqrt((p*(1-p) + z^2/(4*n)) / n)) / denom
    c(center - half, center + half)
  }

  ## 1) Build per-person variables
  dat0 <- df_analysis_filt %>%
    mutate(
      sent_sim0  = to_binary_present(`sim0_Opened_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
      sent_sim05 = to_binary_present(`sim0.5_Opened_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),
      sent_sim1  = to_binary_present(sim1_SuccessfullyDeliveredEmail_TimeStamp),
      sent_sim2  = to_binary_present(sim2_SuccessfullyDeliveredEmail_TimeStamp),

      clicked_sim0  = to_clicked(`sim0_Viewed Landing Page_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
      clicked_sim05 = to_clicked(`sim0.5_Viewed Landing Page_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),
      clicked_sim1  = to_clicked(sim1_EmailLinkClicked_TimeStamp),
      clicked_sim2  = to_clicked(sim2_EmailLinkClicked_TimeStamp),

      clicked_sim0  = clicked_sim0  * sent_sim0,
      clicked_sim05 = clicked_sim05 * sent_sim05,
      clicked_sim1  = clicked_sim1  * sent_sim1,
      clicked_sim2  = clicked_sim2  * sent_sim2,

      compromised_sim0  = to_binary_present(`sim0_Data Entered_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
      compromised_sim05 = to_binary_present(`sim0.5_Data Entered_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),
      compromised_sim1  = to_binary_present(sim1_CredSupplied_TimeStamp_Compromised),
      compromised_sim2  = to_binary_present(sim2_CredSupplied_TimeStamp_Compromised),

      compromised_sim0  = compromised_sim0  * sent_sim0,
      compromised_sim05 = compromised_sim05 * sent_sim05,
      compromised_sim1  = compromised_sim1  * sent_sim1,
      compromised_sim2  = compromised_sim2  * sent_sim2
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      n_sent = sent_sim0 + sent_sim05 + sent_sim1 + sent_sim2,
      n_clicked = clicked_sim0 + clicked_sim05 + clicked_sim1 + clicked_sim2,
      n_compromised = compromised_sim0 + compromised_sim05 + compromised_sim1 + compromised_sim2
    )

  ## only participants with full exposure (4/4)
  df_cc4 <- dat0 %>%
    filter(sent_sim0 == 1, sent_sim05 == 1, sent_sim1 == 1, sent_sim2 == 1) %>%
    mutate(n_sent = 4L)

  cat("N complete exposure (4/4):", nrow(df_cc4), "\n")

  ## 2) Aggregate by number of clicks (0–4), add 0 explicitly
  sumdat <- df_cc4 %>%
    group_by(n_clicked) %>%
    summarise(
      n_people = n(),
      clicks_total = sum(n_clicked, na.rm = TRUE),
      comp_total   = sum(n_compromised, na.rm = TRUE),
      rate_comp_per_click = if_else(clicks_total > 0, comp_total / clicks_total, NA_real_),
      ci_low  = if_else(clicks_total > 0, wilson_ci(comp_total, clicks_total)[1], NA_real_),
      ci_high = if_else(clicks_total > 0, wilson_ci(comp_total, clicks_total)[2], NA_real_),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    complete(n_clicked = 0:4,
             fill = list(n_people = 0, clicks_total = 0, comp_total = 0,
                         rate_comp_per_click = NA_real_, ci_low = NA_real_, ci_high = NA_real_))

  claim("Figure 4: n_people are the bars, rate_comp_per_click with ci_low and ci_high the line")
  print(sumdat)

  k <- max(sumdat$n_people, na.rm = TRUE)

  ## 3) Plot
  p <- ggplot(sumdat, aes(x = factor(n_clicked, levels = 0:4))) +
    geom_col(aes(y = n_people), fill = "grey40", color = "white") +
    geom_line(aes(y = rate_comp_per_click * k, group = 1), linewidth = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(aes(y = rate_comp_per_click * k), size = 3, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_low * k, ymax = ci_high * k), width = 0.10, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "Number of participants",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / k, name = "Compromise probability per click")
    ) +
    labs(x = "Number of phishing emails clicked (0–4)") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 16)

  print(p)

  ## 4) Save
  ggsave(
    "fig4_click_histogram.pdf",
    plot = p, width = 6, height = 4, device = cairo_pdf 
  )

})


```




#Post Hoc Analysis Repeat Clicker (Hierarchical Modelling)
```{r}
## ============================================================
## H4: Repeat-clicker GLMM (4 time points)
## - Outcomes (clicked_*) NOT imputed
## - Predictors only imputed
## ============================================================

section("Post hoc H3: event-level mixed model with detection difficulty",
        "Section 4.4 ('Post-hoc analysis H3'); Table 7 (tab:H3_glmm)",
        note = paste(
          "Called H4 in the code. Logistic model of each click with a random",
          "intercept per participant, m = 30 imputations, pooled by Rubin's",
          "rules. One line per imputation, then the pooled table."))

local({

  View <- function(...) invisible(NULL)

  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(lme4)
  library(mice)
  library(performance)

  set.seed(123)


  to_delivered <- function(x) {
    x <- trimws(as.character(x))
    dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(x) | x == "" ~ 0L,
      x == "--"          ~ 0L,
      TRUE               ~ 1L
    )
  }

  to_clicked <- function(x) {
    x <- trimws(as.character(x))
    dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(x) | x == "" ~ 0L,
      x == "--"          ~ 0L,
      TRUE               ~ 1L
    )
  }

  z <- function(x) as.numeric(scale(x))


  dat0 <- df_analysis_filt


  dat0 <- dat0 %>%
    mutate(
     
      sent_sim0  = to_delivered(`sim0_Opened_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
      sent_sim05 = to_delivered(`sim0.5_Opened_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),
      sent_sim1 = to_delivered(sim1_SuccessfullyDeliveredEmail_TimeStamp),
      sent_sim2 = to_delivered(sim2_SuccessfullyDeliveredEmail_TimeStamp),


      
      clicked_sim0  = to_clicked(`sim0_Viewed Landing Page_Time_c1_2023-03-29`),
      clicked_sim05 = to_clicked(`sim0.5_Viewed Landing Page_Time_c2_2024-07-22`),
      clicked_sim1  = to_clicked(sim1_EmailLinkClicked_TimeStamp),
      clicked_sim2  = to_clicked(sim2_EmailLinkClicked_TimeStamp),

      
      clicked_sim0  = clicked_sim0  * sent_sim0,
      clicked_sim05 = clicked_sim05 * sent_sim05
    )


  dat_h4 <- dat0 %>%
    filter(sent_sim0 == 1, sent_sim05 == 1, sent_sim1 == 1, sent_sim2 == 1)

  cat("H4 base (same delivery filter as main pipeline) | N =", nrow(dat_h4), "\n")


  want <- c(
    "clicked_sim0","clicked_sim05","clicked_sim1","clicked_sim2",
    "optimism_bias","risk_perception","negative_emotions","acceptance",
    "self_efficacy","locus_of_control","feeling_attacked","per_orga_security",
    "age_num","gender_bin","JobRole_bin","anonymisedEmail"
  )
  dat_h4 <- dat_h4[, intersect(want, names(dat_h4)), drop = FALSE]


  if ("JobRole_bin" %in% names(dat_h4)) dat_h4$JobRole_bin <- factor(dat_h4$JobRole_bin)

  if ("gender_bin" %in% names(dat_h4)) {
    
    x <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(dat_h4$gender_bin)))
    x[!x %in% c(0L, 1L)] <- NA_integer_
    dat_h4$gender_bin <- factor(x, levels = c(0, 1))
  }


  click_vars <- intersect(c("clicked_sim0","clicked_sim05","clicked_sim1","clicked_sim2"), names(dat_h4))

  dat_h4[click_vars] <- lapply(dat_h4[click_vars], function(x) {
    x <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(x)))
    x[!x %in% c(0L, 1L)] <- NA_integer_
    x
  })

  cat("Unique IDs:", dplyr::n_distinct(dat_h4$anonymisedEmail), "\n")

  dat_h4 <- dat_h4 %>% filter(if_all(all_of(click_vars), ~ !is.na(.x)))
  cat("H4 complete outcomes (all 4 cycles observed) | N =", nrow(dat_h4), "\n")


  meth <- make.method(dat_h4)
  pred <- make.predictorMatrix(dat_h4)


  if ("anonymisedEmail" %in% names(dat_h4)) {
    meth["anonymisedEmail"] <- ""
    pred[, "anonymisedEmail"] <- 0
    pred["anonymisedEmail", ] <- 0
  }


  meth[click_vars] <- ""
  pred[, click_vars] <- 0


  for (v in intersect(c("age_num","gender_bin","JobRole_bin"), names(dat_h4))) {
    meth[v] <- ""
  }


  for (v in intersect(c("optimism_bias","risk_perception","negative_emotions",
                        "acceptance","self_efficacy","locus_of_control",
                        "feeling_attacked","per_orga_security"), names(dat_h4))) {
    meth[v] <- "pmm"
  }

  stopifnot(identical(names(meth), colnames(dat_h4)))

  imp <- mice(
    dat_h4,
    m = 30,
    method = meth,
    predictorMatrix = pred,
    maxit = 30,
    seed = 123,
    printFlag = FALSE
  )
  cat("Imputation finished (predictors only).\n")


  fits <- vector("list", imp$m)
  
  icc_vals <- numeric(imp$m)


  for (i in 1:imp$m) {

    d <- complete(imp, i)
    d$id <- factor(d$anonymisedEmail)

    if ("JobRole_bin" %in% names(d)) d$JobRole_bin <- factor(d$JobRole_bin)


    for (v in c("optimism_bias","risk_perception","negative_emotions","acceptance",
                "self_efficacy","locus_of_control","age_num",
                "feeling_attacked","per_orga_security")) {
      if (v %in% names(d) && is.numeric(d[[v]])) d[[v]] <- z(d[[v]])
    }

    long_i <- d %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = all_of(click_vars),
        names_to = "cycle",
        values_to = "clicked_bin"
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        cycle = factor(
          cycle,
          levels = c("clicked_sim0","clicked_sim05","clicked_sim1","clicked_sim2"),
          labels = c("sim0","sim0.5","sim1","sim2")
        ),
        clicked_bin = as.integer(clicked_bin),
        difficulty = case_when(
          cycle == "sim0"   ~ 1L,
          cycle == "sim0.5" ~ 2L,
          cycle == "sim1"   ~ 2L,
          cycle == "sim2"   ~ 3L
        )
      )

    rhs <- c(
      "difficulty",
      intersect(
        c("optimism_bias","risk_perception","negative_emotions","acceptance",
          "self_efficacy","locus_of_control","feeling_attacked","per_orga_security",
          "age_num","gender_bin","JobRole_bin"),
        names(long_i)
      )
    )

    form <- as.formula(paste("clicked_bin ~", paste(rhs, collapse = " + "), "+ (1 | id)"))

    fits[[i]] <- glmer(
      form,
      data = long_i,
      family = binomial("logit"),
      control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
    )

    icc_vals[i] <- performance::icc(fits[[i]])$ICC_adjusted

    
    r2_vals <- performance::r2_nakagawa(fits[[i]])
    cat(sprintf("Imputation %d: R2_marg = %.3f, R2_cond = %.3f\n",
                i, r2_vals$R2_marginal, r2_vals$R2_conditional))
  }


  betas <- lapply(fits, fixef)
  Vlist <- lapply(fits, vcov)
  m <- length(betas)

  coef_names <- names(betas[[1]])
  Q <- sapply(betas, function(b) setNames(b[coef_names], coef_names))

  qbar <- rowMeans(Q)
  Ubar <- Reduce("+", Vlist) / m
  Q_centered <- sweep(Q, 1, qbar, "-")
  B <- (Q_centered %*% t(Q_centered)) / (m - 1)
  Tmat <- Ubar + (1 + 1/m) * B

  se <- sqrt(diag(Tmat))
  zval <- qbar / se
  p <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(zval))

  out <- data.frame(
    term      = coef_names,
    estimate  = qbar,
    se        = se,
    z         = zval,
    p         = p,
    OR        = exp(qbar),
    OR_low95  = exp(qbar - 1.96 * se),
    OR_high95 = exp(qbar + 1.96 * se),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      p_fmt = format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-3),
      OR_ci = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", OR, OR_low95, OR_high95)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(term, estimate, se, z, p = p_fmt, OR_ci)

  claim("Table 7: estimate, se and p below. Section 4.4: difficulty beta = 0.83, z = 4.64, OR = 2.30")
  cat("\n--- H4 pooled fixed effects (Rubin's rules; outcomes not imputed) ---\n")
  print(out, digits = 3)


  assign("dat_h4", dat_h4, envir = .GlobalEnv)


assign("icc_vals", icc_vals, envir = .GlobalEnv)
assign("fits", fits, envir = .GlobalEnv)


  
})

claim("Section 4.4: individual differences account for about 16 % of the variance: the mean ICC, then its SD and range")
mean(icc_vals)
sd(icc_vals)
range(icc_vals)


```




#Qualitative data analysis
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

section("Self-reported reasons for clicking; Figure 6",
        "Section 4.5; Figure 6 (fig:selfreportedreasons), written to results/fig6_selfreportedreasons.pdf",
        note = paste(
          "Cohen's kappa and the seven open-text counts are derived in",
          "results/qualitative.log. The first table is every combination of",
          "the multi-select item as answered."))


library(dplyr)

df_analysis_filt %>%
  count(reasons_click, sort = TRUE)





###

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)

## -------------------
## 1) Closed-format options
## -------------------
df_predef_raw <- tribble(
  ~raw, ~n,
  "legitimate", 39,
  "Other reason:", 23,
  "I clicked on the link to find out if the e-mail was phishing", 4,
  "Our security system would protect me from any harm", 6,
  "I did not read the e-mail content and just clicked the link", 3
)

claim("Section 4.5 and Figure 6: 39 / 6 / 4 / 3, typed into the figure code as submitted: the n column below, ",
      "leaving out the 'Other reason:' row")
print(df_predef_raw)

## The same counts derived from the multi-select item, as the camera-ready
## version does. Only 39 differs: the data give 40, and 39 was a manual entry
## error (see README.md, Known limitations). The figure keeps the submitted 39.
reasons_sel <- df_analysis_filt$reasons_click
reasons_sel <- reasons_sel[!is.na(reasons_sel) & reasons_sel != ""]
n_reason <- function(option) sum(grepl(option, reasons_sel, fixed = TRUE))
claim("Not in the submitted paper: the same counts derived from the data, respondents = 67")
print(tribble(
  ~raw, ~n,
  "legitimate",                                                   n_reason("thought that the e-mail was legitimate"),
  "Other reason:",                                                n_reason("Other reason:"),
  "I clicked on the link to find out if the e-mail was phishing", n_reason("to find out if the e-mail was phishing"),
  "Our security system would protect me from any harm",           n_reason("security system would protect me from any harm"),
  "I did not read the e-mail content and just clicked the link",  n_reason("did not read the e-mail content and just clicked the link")
))

df_predef <- df_predef_raw %>%
  mutate(raw = as.character(raw)) %>%
  mutate(
    reason = str_squish(raw),
    reason = str_replace_all(reason, "\\s*:\\s*$", ""),
    reason = case_when(
      tolower(reason) == "legitimate" ~ "Thought email was legitimate",
      TRUE ~ reason
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(reason) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(tolower(reason) != "other reason") %>%
  mutate(group = "Closed-format options")

## -------------------
## 2) Open-text (Other reasons)
## -------------------
df_other_codes <- tibble(
  reason = c(
    "Situational fit",
    "Distracted / stressed / multitasking",
    "On mobile device",
    "Seemed legitimate / curiosity",
    "Did not expect phishing",
    "Did not know how to differentiate",
    "Not marked as external"
  ),
  n = c(13, 12, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1),
  group = "Open-text (Other reasons)"
)

## -------------------
## 3) Combine + order within facets
## -------------------
df_all <- bind_rows(df_predef, df_other_codes) %>%
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = c("Closed-format options", "Open-text (Other reasons)"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(group, desc(n)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  mutate(reason = factor(reason, levels = rev(unique(reason)))) %>%  # order within each facet
  ungroup()

## -------------------
## 4) Plot (horizontal facet headers)
## -------------------
p_list <- ggplot(df_all, aes(x = reason, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey30", width = 0.75) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  facet_wrap(~ group, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of participants") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10, b = 10, l = 20)
  )

print(p_list)

ggsave(
  "fig6_selfreportedreasons.pdf",
  plot = p_list,
  width = 6.2,
  height = 4.8,
  units = "in",
  device = cairo_pdf
)
 

```
